message:
Pass LC_ALL=C to sort, when generating HTTP headers

Summary:
sort's output varies depending on the locale (LC_COLLATE in
particular). Pass LC_ALL=C when calling sort, to avoid adding a
locale-based variance to the build. This makes proxygen
reproducible-friendly.

See https://reproducible-builds.org/docs/locales/ for more.
Closes https://github.com/facebook/proxygen/pull/82

message:
fix(chroot): use locales-all; LC_ALL=C in post_commands; direct locale file write

locales-all ships all locales pre-compiled so locale-gen is not needed.
Replacing 'locales' + locale-gen + update-locale with locales-all +
a direct printf to /etc/default/locale avoids the Perl-based update-locale
which fails mid-chroot-build due to locale env vars inherited from the host.

apply_post_commands now sets LC_ALL=C alongside DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
so Perl-based tools inside the chroot don't emit spurious locale warnings
regardless of what the build host's locale is.

fix(agentic-patterns): make debate convergence locale-independent (#6484)

## Issue

`ConvergenceStrategy.unanimousLastWord()` compares the last word of each
debater's position after upper-casing it with the **default locale**:

```java
String lastWord = tokens[tokens.length - 1]
        .replaceAll("^[^\\p{Alnum}]+|[^\\p{Alnum}]+$", "")
        .toUpperCase();
```

On a JVM running in the Turkish (or Azeri) locale,
`"disagree".toUpperCase()` is `"DİSAGREE"` (dotted capital I) while
`"DISAGREE".toUpperCase()` stays `"DISAGREE"`. Two debaters that reach
the same verdict in different cases therefore never converge, and the
debate runs to its maximum number of rounds.

## Change

- `toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)` — the verdict is data used for comparison,
not text shown to a user.
- A test that runs under the Turkish locale and restores the default
afterwards, following the pattern of the other locale tests in this
repository.

## General checklist

- [x] There are no breaking changes
- [x] I have added unit and integration tests for my change
- [ ] I have manually run all the unit and integration tests in the
module I have added/changed, and they are all green

> The tests in this PR were not run locally (no JDK available on the
machine I prepared this on), so I am relying on CI here. Happy to
iterate on anything it flags, including formatting.

[SPARK-48682][SQL][FOLLOW-UP] Changed initCap behaviour with UTF8_BINARY collation

### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Changing the way that spark does initCap with respect to UTF8_BINARY collation.
In this PR, initCap titlecases the first character of every word, and lowercases every other character. Words are separated only by ASCII space.
Special care is taken when lowercasing Σ, to take into account if it is at the end of the word(with respect to case-ignorable characters) and should be lowercased into ς, or in other case into σ(this already works correctly with the current implementation because lowercasing a whole string handled this, but in this PR this was handled manually because lowercase function wasn't used).

The key difference between outputs that this PR introduces is:
| input | current_initCap(input) | new_initCap(input) |
|----------|----------|----------|
| İo   | İo (I\u0307o)  | İo   |
| ß ﬁ ﬃ ﬀ ﬆ    | ß ﬁ ﬃ ﬀ ﬆ   | Ss Fi Ffi Ff St   |

These are just some examples, much more mappings are actually affected.
More details about the key changes are in the next section.
This behaviour is put under the ICU_CASE_MAPPINGS_ENABLED flag in SQLConf, which is true by default.

### Why are the changes needed?

The previous implementation first lowercases the complete string, and then titlecases the first character of every word[1].
When titlecasing the first character of every word, it maps a single codepoint to a single codepoint[2].

fix(F1): make block-sequence "- " StartsWith checks ordinal

trimmed.StartsWith("- ") (4 sites in YamlParser.cs: ParseNode,
ParseMapping, ParseSequence, LineIsSequenceItem) used the string
overload with no StringComparison, defaulting to CurrentCulture -- a
linguistic comparison that treats zero-width format characters like
U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN as ignorable. Empirically "­- x".StartsWith("- ")
is true under CurrentCulture/InvariantCulture but false under Ordinal
(the byte-exact comparison Rust's str::starts_with always uses),
causing such a line to be misread as a block-sequence item instead of
a plain scalar. Add StringComparison.Ordinal at all 4 sites.
StartsWith also needs to use StringComparison.Ordinal

message:
fix(ci): pin LC_ALL=C for manifest sort (#207)

generate-manifest.sh sorted git ls-files under the ambient locale, so a
contributor on a UTF-8 locale produced a different collation order than
CI (C.UTF-8) and tripped the manifest-completeness check. Pin the sort to
LC_ALL=C so the manifest is reproducible regardless of contributor locale.

message:
Turkish i defense in java
http://codereview.appspot.com/6300084

Because of the Turkish 'i', String#toLowerCase etc are unsafe to use.
We have Strings.toLowerCase etc that are safe, but they aren't used
universally.

This patch does:

- rename Strings.toLowerCase etc to Strings.lower etc, so that it's
easier to use a simple grep to find stray uses of the unsafe methods.

- add a shell script tools/codecheck.sh that complains if the unsafe
methods get used.  "ant runtests" will run codecheck.

- fix all uses of the unsafe methods.

- replace hand-coded loops in Strings.lower etc with standard calls
using Locale.ENGLISH, because it's less code to worry about.  This
behaves differently for non-ASCII characters, but we don't care as
long as it's consistent and isn't confused by Turkish 'i' issues.

R=ihab.awad@gmail.com

在 IDatabase 中的 NameFormats 枚举中，添加了一个新的枚举值 None，表示保持原样，并将 Default 的描述从“原样”改为“默认”。

Set LC_ALL=C when using sed on a binary file

Because some sed implementations, at least the one on macOS, detect
invalid text in the current locale's encoding and error out. See:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/19242275/re-error-illegal-byte-sequence-on-mac-os-x

This makes the script work on macOS.

perf: replace ToUpper()+StartsWith() with OrdinalIgnoreCase comparisons (#282)

Eliminates heap allocations in the MHTML parser hot paths and MetricsGetter
by replacing the pattern `str.ToUpper().StartsWith("KEY")` with
`str.StartsWith("KEY", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)`.

This avoids creating a temporary uppercase string for every comparison,
reducing GC pressure when parsing MHTML files with many MIME headers.

fix(tls): use locale-independent ASCII comparison for SNI hostname matching (#2515)

Replace strcasecmp() with custom ascii_strcasecmp() for SNI certificate
lookup to ensure consistent behavior across all locales, per RFC 4343.

The previous implementation used strcasecmp() which has locale-dependent
behavior on some systems (e.g., Turkish locale where 'i' uppercases to
'İ' instead of 'I'). This could cause SNI hostname matching to fail
unexpectedly.

Changes:
- Add ascii_strcasecmp() static function implementing RFC 4343 ASCII
  case folding
- Replace strcasecmp() call in find_sni_cert_index() with
  ascii_strcasecmp()
- Remove unused strings.h include

Closes #2359

Reduce String allocations

- Replace String with SmolStr in config and hot-path maps
- Replace String with Cow<'_, str> where ownership is not always
  required
- Replace to_lowercase and to_ascii_lowercase with to_lowercase_cow and
  to_ascii_lowercase_cow from str-utils.
- Replace format!() + into() to SmolStr with format_smolstr!
- Other minor improvements.
